correctness.rationale: Norm C follows from coordinatewise Lipschitz upper bounds and pointwise directional derivatives. Finite-coordinate holomorphic symbols have compact free-space linearizations by Bayart--Lemay--Petitjean Theorem 4.1. Uniform Cauchy bounds on the evaluation second derivative on radius r<1 yield ||T-T_N||<=sup_{j>N} c_j + K_r C eta_N with eta_N->0. For every compact K, unit derivative evaluation vectors at escape coordinates, followed by barycenter, force ||T-K||>=limsup c_j. These arguments cover all finite 1<=p<infinity and boundary cases L=0, C=0. The concrete finite checker passed 2080 supplementary assertions, not an infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The exact Calkin norm is the natural quantitative refinement of the 2026 weak-versus-norm-compactness dichotomy for holomorphic-Lipschitz-free operators. It completely classifies compactness and the sharp positive defect across the entire separated-coordinate family, yields every normalized essential-norm ratio in [0,1], and separates weak compactness in reflexive ell_p targets. These quantities are not recovered from one isolated monomial example or a simple renaming of the published zero-distance criterion.
